+waste: the file is read again by every role that implements or reviews the
+feature. -->

 # Requirements — Wishlist

+<!-- What this feature is for, in two or three sentences: the need it answers

+
 ## Requirements
 
-### REQ-004 — Wishlist holds items
+<!-- Each requirement follows this structure:
 
-A shopper keeps items on a list without buying them.
+### REQ-### — <short title>
+- **Description:** <what is required, from the business/user perspective> ^req-###
+- **Conditions of satisfaction:**
+  - <happy path: given <state>, when <action>, then <observable outcome>>
+  - Error: when <invalid input or failure>, then <error response>
+  - Edge: when <boundary case>, then <expected behaviour>
 
-- Error: an item already on the list is not added twice.
+Requirements describe *what* and *why*, never *how*.
+One behaviour per condition — "and" inside a condition means it should be split.
+At least two conditions per requirement, one of them an `Error:` condition.
 
-### REQ-005 — Move to cart
+The `^req-###` at the end of the description line is the requirement's anchor,
+the id in lower case — `REQ-ACC-003` gives `^req-acc-003`. It is what
+`design.md` and `tasks.md` link to, so it is written even where nothing points
+at it yet. A term this feature defines is marked ==like this== where it is
+defined, once, and used plainly everywhere after.
+-->
 
-A shopper moves an item from the list into the cart.
+## Assumptions
 
-- Error: an item that is out of stock stays on the list.

+
+<!-- Points only the human can settle, one line each — see
+`.sdd/protocols/spec-modes.md`. -->

+<!-- Each task follows this structure:
 
-- [ ] **TASK-002** — Move an item into the cart
-  - **Requires:** REQ-005
-  - **Type:** backend
-  - **Description:** The service method behind the endpoint.
+- [ ] **TASK-001** — <short title>
+  - **Requires:** [REQ-001](new-requirements.md#^req-001), [REQ-003](new-requirements.md#^req-003)
+  - **Type:** backend | frontend
+  - **Description:** <what to implement, technical details, acceptance criteria>
+
+The order of the list is the order of execution. A requirement is written as a
+link to its anchor in `new-requirements.md` — the id itself stays in the link
+text, so a reader with no vault open still reads `REQ-001`.
+
+A done task is `- [x]`. A blocked task stays unchecked, keeps its ID and its
+title, and carries the reason at the end of the line:
+
+- [ ] **TASK-007** — <short title> — BLOCKED: <one-line reason>
+-->
